scope: Project logs, snapshots and research metadata audited; private/operator/inbox/credential paths excluded. Lossless archive affects closed untracked artifacts>=24h/32KiB; tracked financial/case records, receipts, hardlinks, current aliases and open files excluded. All original bytes remain recoverable by hash; no age expiry.

audit.notable_suffix_caution: One historical .body.gz actually contains plain TSV; storage reader uses gzip magic, not suffix.

future.discovery_snapshot: Compact UTF-8 JSON + deterministic gzip6; raw and gzip SHA, full criteria/counts/coverage and byte counts. Plain opt-out retained. Latest aliases point to actual gzip; consumers use compression-aware loader.
future.batch_context: One compressed compact JSON parent per scan; --input FILE.json.gz --batch-index N reads one unit without source/network calls. --reference-only stores parent path/decoded SHA plus selected batch, avoiding repeated policy/source metadata. Pretty/Markdown views remain optional.

markdown_scaffold_audit.finding: Repeated group scaffolds were23.63%; top preambles were once per scan, not per batch.

future.maintenance: Existing scheduled check-ins archive<=128files/64MiB input/30s; event ticks skip. No additional timer. Active daemon logs stay open and are not renamed/truncated; they were18.6MiB, versus~1.5GiB closed evidence/data.

verification.crash_tail_policy: Readers retain complete prior mappings after an interrupted append. Locked maintenance preserves an uncommitted tail separately before truncation; complete corrupt/conflicting records fail closed.

limits: Archived artifact checks prove byte preservation, not source truth or historical completeness. No valuation, forecast, count, account or trade changed. Existing live append logs were audited but not rotated; persistent descriptors need a separate reopen-aware change if growth becomes material.
